# ALTER COLUMN SET DEFAULT on parameterized columns: the emulator checks a literal default
# against the column's type parameters and rejects it when they do not hold. BigQuery's
# documentation does not say whether it checks them when the default is set. Each script
# reports "ok" or the error, and drops the dataset it creates.
DECLARE result STRING;
CREATE SCHEMA bqanswers_alter_default_string;
CREATE TABLE bqanswers_alter_default_string.t (name STRING(8));
BEGIN
  ALTER TABLE bqanswers_alter_default_string.t ALTER COLUMN name SET DEFAULT 'too long for the column';
  SET result = 'ok';
EXCEPTION WHEN ERROR THEN
  SET result = 'error: ' || @@error.message;
END;
DROP SCHEMA bqanswers_alter_default_string CASCADE;
SELECT result
?>

DECLARE result STRING;
CREATE SCHEMA bqanswers_alter_default_numeric;
CREATE TABLE bqanswers_alter_default_numeric.t (n NUMERIC(5, 2));
BEGIN
  ALTER TABLE bqanswers_alter_default_numeric.t ALTER COLUMN n SET DEFAULT NUMERIC '1000';
  SET result = 'ok';
EXCEPTION WHEN ERROR THEN
  SET result = 'error: ' || @@error.message;
END;
DROP SCHEMA bqanswers_alter_default_numeric CASCADE;
SELECT result
?>
